decisions.reason: The adjustable feature may still offer upside and the cost to keep the cardboard display option open is low, so real options reasoning favors keeping it.
Its pegboard back serves a niche retail need and the option remains cheap to hold, so management keeps it while uncertainty persists.
As a standard quarter-pallet display, it is a core, low-cost option with likely stable demand, making abandonment unlikely.
The eighth-pallet format is a low-cost variant that retains option value for smaller retail spaces, so it is kept.
A wooden display pallet lies outside the firm's paper core, has higher keeping costs, and after four years its option value is unlikely to justify further commitment, so it is dropped.
The media-specific display targets a declining retail segment, so the option's upside has likely resolved negatively, and dropping frees resources for more promising options.
